A B S T R A C T
Numerous developing countries are currently grappling with energy crises due to the current surge in
global fossil fuels prices. This situation has prompted policymakers and cities administrator to urgently seek
alternative power sources. Scientists worldwide are actively working on innovative computational methods
to address the coordination challenges faced by hybrid power systems. Their objective is to optimize the
utilization of environmentally friendly hybrid power sources, such as clean energy sources (CESs) like wind
and solar power, within the framework of traditional hydro-thermal coordination. This research aims to
examine how integrating CESs into conventional energy delivering hydro-thermal coordination model can
minimize the significant costs associated with energy production. The proposed approach involves constructing
a probabilistic model to represent the hybrid energy coordination problem. To handle uncertainties related
to CESs, a technique known as point estimation is employed. This technique employs Weibull and Beta
distribution functions to handle uncertain input variables associated with wind and solar power. The present
study employs an optimization paradigm that integrates the black widow optimization (BWO) algorithm
with the radial basis function neural network (RBFNN). This paradigm not only considers the uncertainties
in the system but also adapts its parameters to attain an optimum balance among the exploration as well
as exploitation phase. Within the context of advancing energy transition the outcomes of our simulations
demonstrate a significant achievement. The incorporation of CESs into the hydro-thermal coordination problem
yields a substantial 10 percent reduction in operational costs and an impressive 64 percent decline in emissions.
The convergence curves of the proposed scheme reveal that the presented hybrid computing paradigm quickly
converges to the optimal solution, attaining the best global optimum solution. Three case studies have
been conducted, in Case Study-I, the best attained optimal cost and emissions are $3.6e4/day and 2.8e4
lb/day, respectively, with photovoltaic and wind energy costs at $1148/day and $3055/day, respectively.
For Case Study-II, a complex function, emissions of 15887.42 lb/day and an energy production cost of
$26072.89/day are achieved. For Case Study-III, the optimal cost of $26558/day and emissions of 12932 lb/day
are acquired using the proposed approach. This valuable research contribution holds particular significance for
the economic empowerment of developing nations. By diminishing their reliance on imported fossil fuels for
energy generation, it paves the way for enhanced self-sufficiency. Moreover, the findings provide a well-defined
pathway towards fostering sustainable and environmentally friendly energy production within urban settings.
Additionally, the research highlights the transition from fossil fuel-dependent industries to the establishment
of sustainable urban economies.

Cities are experiencing a greater demand for energy as a result of
global growing cities, which has pulled existing infrastructures and
escalated ecological problems to fulfil the United Nation Sustainable
Development Goals (SDG) such as SDG 13. Urban centres must use
clean energy sources (CESs) to reduce global warming, improve air
quality, and meet ecological objectives (Singh et al., 2023). This study
aims to explore challenges related to transitioning energy sources in
urban environments. Coordination of hybrid power infrastructure is a
common optimization task in this industry. Solar and wind generation
are intermittent, thus utility administrators must carefully incorporate
stable energy sources. This compensates for power shortages and maxi-
mizes power utilization during peak production. Simultaneously, power
dispatch facilities have a responsibility to reduce the costs associated
with transitioning among multiple sources of power throughout the
execution of this operation (Ahmed et al., 2022d).
The primary objective of this study is to develop a sophisticated
optimization paradigm based on soft computing strategies. This study
presents an approach that employs the black widow algorithm for
optimization purposes. This approach is employed to tackle an intricate
planning challenge that involves the integration of energy facilities
for hydroelectricity, thermo-electric units, photovoltaic facilities, and
wind energy facilities. This paradigm aims to overcome the challenges
hindering the adoption of electrical power in urban settings while also
promoting cost-effectiveness and ecologically sustainable practices. The
primary aim of this study is to mitigate the expenses associated with
electric power production as well as the release of GHG pollutants from
thermal power plants within a certain period. Utilizing readily avail-
able and affordable energy sources like hydroelectric, wind, and solar
power will help achieve this. Furthermore, zero carbon plans in green
integration promote the widespread use and incorporation of clean
energy sources in order to establish a carbon-neutral or emissions-free
power industry and mitigate climate change. The issue at hand might
be characterized as a multifaceted and constrained energy optimization
challenge. The findings of this study will make a valuable contribu-
tion to the advancement of urban planning, power management, and
policy development. Furthermore, this will enhance the resilience and
livability of cities for present and prospective residents.
1.2. Literature review

pertaining to soft computing algorithms employed for addressing the
energy dispatch problem with present work. For better use of solar
energy in power networks, Stephen et al. Afonaa-Mensah et al. (2023)
explored strategy to reduce variability in solar resources. A full day

Nevertheless, it is important to note that this study overlooked two
significant non-convex constraints, namely, restricted operating regions
and transmission losses. In the investigation cited as Basak et al. (2023),

optimal solution for operational costs in energy networks. The study
utilized both the crow search and JAYA algorithms to address various
network load scenarios, considering a linear profile for wind energy. It
is important to note, however, that this research overlooked system-
associated constraints and demonstrated suboptimal performance in
addressing the uncertainties associated with green energy sources.
Several other studies, including those referenced as Sheng et al. (2023),
Sundaram (2022), have explored single and dual optimization functions
for dispatch models to achieve the optimal solution for the generation
cost of hybrid energy networks. The comparative analysis, as illustrated
in Table 1, indicates that the model presented in this work is both more
intricate and practical. This is attributed to its consideration of practical
constraints and the development of an efficient approach to handle the
uncertainties linked with CESs.
The optimization of electric power efficiency is a fundamental
problem in the context of contemporary urban building projects, ex-
erting a significant influence on the long-term viability and robustness
of cities. Some other applications of optimization can be observed
in waste management (Alruqi and Sharma, 2023), the synthesis of
biohydrogen (Sharma et al., 2023a), and theoretical frameworks for
chemical splittings (Sharma et al., 2023b). In recent times, scholars
have employed a wide range of techniques to confront the challenge
of engineering optimization in the domain of energy delivery and ef-
fective utilization (Zhang et al., 2023; Alzahrani et al., 2023). Recently,
traditional convex optimization techniques are implemented to address
a range of planning challenges. These strategies encompass linear pro-
gramming, which utilizes computational frameworks to optimize linear
objectives while adhering to linear limitations (Lauinger et al., 2016).
Conversely, Lagrange relaxation entails the relaxation of limitations to
simplify complex optimization issues in electric cars (Adacher et al.,
2023). Furthermore, mixed-integer programming integrates both con-
tinuous and discrete decision variables in optimization models, which
improves its adaptability in CESs consumption for distributed energy
networks (Huang et al., 2022). Optimizing scheduling solutions also
uses gradient search procedures, which are a type of iterative improve-
ment based on the gradient of an objective function (Vijayalakshmi
et al., 2022). These conventional approaches serve as fundamental tools
for addressing the intricate task of optimizing schedules across various

In the past decade, a multitude of algorithmic evolution and compu-
tational techniques based on swarm intelligence have been employed
for addressing traditional scheduling dilemmas and nonetheless, each
of these methods has its own limitations and benefits (Mishra and
Kane, 2023). For example, evolutionary optimization framework gar-
nered significant attention as well as applause owing to their inherent
adaptability and reliability in effectively discerning the most suitable
options (Abdelkader et al., 2022). The application of evolutionary
algorithms to tackle optimal planning challenges in various domains
encompasses: urban planning (Jiang et al., 2023), aerospace engineer-
ing (Periaux and Tuovinen, 2023), power system operations (Ahmed
et al., 2022b), buildings structural design (Dixit and Stefańska, 2023),
and transportation (Ahmed et al., 2023c). Currently, there is a no-
table emphasis among academics on the utilization of population
based intelligence-driven algorithms and meta-heuristic soft computa-
tional optimization approaches. This is due to their robustness and in-
creased effectiveness in tackling complex multi-dimensional restrictions
and real-world engineering problems. The utilization of these algo-
rithms to address power coordination issues manifests are: artificial bee
colony (Hakli, 2023), bacterial foraging optimization (Li et al., 2022),
krill herd algorithm (Hu et al., 2022), and whale optimization (Ahmed
et al., 2022a).
Meta-heuristic techniques offer a greater potential for circumvent-
ing local optima and uncovering the optimal global solution, and
numerous studies from researchers worldwide have been documented
concerning the power scheduling problems for sustainable urban power
consumption. Hammid et al. (2023) performed a comprehensive anal-
ysis and comparison of several approaches utilized in dealing with
the hydro-thermal scheduling problem (HTSP). In the modern era,
there has been an increasing inclination towards proposing hybridized
fundamental algorithms as a means to address the challenges posed
by HTSP. An example of a hybrid approach was introduced by Bal-
achander et al. (2022), which combines a bacterial foraging algorithm
with a particle swarm technique to tackle the problem of HTSP. This
approach takes into account the complex constraints that arise from the
chronological interconnections of plants and the consequences of valve-
point loading effect limitations. The authors of Ghosh et al. (2019)
utilized the ABC-BAT algorithm in tandem to tackle the problem of the
HTSP. The research conducted by the authors encompassed two unique
approaches: one strategy aimed at minimizing costs, while the other
strategy focused on improving the general efficiency of the system.
While hybrid methods indeed offer improved convergence, they fall
short in terms of computational resource efficiency. Additionally, these
hybrid strategies present greater implementation challenges compared
to alternative approaches.
The global popularity of wind and solar energy is increasing owing
to its cost-effectiveness and ecologically sustainable characteristics. In
comparison to the situation a decade ago, there has been a notable
increase in the percentage of worldwide energy consumption derived
from CES, rising from 8% to 18.3% in the year 2015 (Heaton et al.,
2023). Within the context of present-day urban planning, there is
a compelling need to adopt a more strategic approach towards the
utilization of CESs (Khavarian-Garmsir et al., 2023). This need arises
not only from the desire to achieve cost efficiency but also from
the aspiration to attain the lofty objective of completely eliminating
carbon emissions (Kasaeian et al., 2023). The prevailing trend in power
infrastructure development highlights the imminent transition towards
the prioritization of clean energy consumption. The integration of green
power systems into conventional power scheduling paradigms has been
driven by a common worldwide concern shared by energy managers
and urban planners (Meraj et al., 2023). Nevertheless, the incorporation
of this integration adds a new level of complexity to existing energy
models. The complexity associated with sustainable energy sources
provide intrinsic limitations that standard optimization methods are not
well suited to handle. Consequently, there exists a significant deficiency
in the capacity of conventional optimization techniques to provide
all-encompassing techno-economic solutions that are imperative for
effectively addressing the complexities of the contemporary energy
environment (Chu et al., 2023).
Upon doing a full analysis of the literature described above, it
becomes apparent that there exists a noticeable gap. This gap presents
an opportunity for the development and implementation of a composite
energy planning model. The objective of this model is to function as
a flexible and comprehensive solution that can effectively tackle the
complex issues associated with energy production in several domains.

work for Hydro-Thermal-Solar-Wind Planning (HTSWP) by employing

This research also addresses grid stability, market dynamics, risk as-

to generate clean energy. The creation of this model possesses a double

crucial role in promoting the adoption of sustainable energy strategies
in urban environments, hence generating significant consequences for
a wide range of interested parties, such as politicians, urban planners,
industry leaders, and local communities. The major contributions of
this study are as follows:
1. This study distinguishes itself from previous scholarly publica-
tions (Das et al., 2018; Yaşar and Özyön, 2020) by specifically
addressing a new hydro-thermal scheduling problem that in-
corporates an extra aim related to thermal plant emissions. In
order to enhance the genuineness and applicability of the model,
this work integrates two supplementary constraints: spinning
reserves and restricted operation zones, hence distinguishing it
from prior research (Kumar and Dhillon, 2022; Dasgupta et al.,
2020a). Implementing the HTSWP coordination idea improves
the energy generation of eco-friendly power sources and si-
multaneously decreases greenhouse gas emissions from thermal
power plants. This paradigm enables urban planners and energy
managers to effectively accomplish their long-term objectives
related to the environment, society, and finances.
2. The hybrid black widow search method has been suggested as a
possible strategy for efficiently addressing the multi-dimensional
coordination problem in HTSWP. This strategy showcases pro-
ficiency in efficiently handling intricate multi-dimensional con-
strained optimization issues, hence establishing itself as a novel
and successful optimization technique. Compared to previous
attempts (Dasgupta et al., 2022, 2020b), the suggested optimiza-
tion framework exhibits enhanced adaptability, leading to more
precise optimal solutions with reduced computational require-
ments. Furthermore, the sine cosine optimization framework
(SCOF) used in prior research lacks robust adaptive capabilities
to dynamically adjust its parameters in real-time during the
optimization process.
3. This study introduces new ideas and innovative approach that
attempt to speed up the transition to CESs and enhance energy
utilization. A novel framework is suggested to enhance the mod-
elling of uncertain energy dynamics of CESs. This framework
integrates the point-estimation technique (PET) with RETscreen
meteorological data. This distinctive attribute has the capacity to
propel progress in urban design, energy management, and policy
development, leading to the construction of more resilient and
habitable cities for current and future generations.
The structure of this paper is outlined in following manner. Sec-
tion 2 discusses the mathematical modelling of HTSWP. Section 3
discusses the PET for CESs uncertainty modelling. The HTSWP com-
puting paradigm is presented in Section 4, while Section 5 provides
details on the RETScreen software. Section 6 covers the simulation
results. Finally, Section 7 presents the conclusion and future research
directions.
2. HTSWP mathematical modelling
The main goal of the HTSWP initiative is to reduce operating
costs related to energy generation and mitigate pollutants arising from
the combustion of fuel in energy hubs. Furthermore, this paradigm
facilitates the utilization of environmentally friendly and economically
feasible options for energy generation for urban infrastructure.
This part presents the mathematical representation of the research’s
layout, with the goal of achieving power output equilibrium among
energy production hubs, while taking into consideration system limita-
tions. Every individual energy source is quantitatively classified based
on its unique constraints during a certain time period. Let us examine
a hybrid power network comprising 𝑁𝑇 thermo-electric generators,
𝑁𝐻 hydro-electric units, 𝑁𝑆 photovoltaic power modules, and 𝑁𝑊
wind generators. The hybrid configuration presented in this study
is specifically engineered to function during a time period denoted
as 𝑇 hours. During this length, the configuration aims to optimize
the generation of power schedules by effectively using carbon-free
sources. The main goals of this design are to utilize the sustainable
energy option while reducing running costs of power network and
also minimize the discharge of GHGs. Moreover, the reservoir capacity
of each hydro-electric unit, photovoltaic system and wind units are
strategically adjusted to its utmost potential, guaranteeing that the
generated power schedule seamlessly coincides with the pre-established
urban load-demand needs.

4.2. Black widow optimization approach for training RBFNNs
Swarm intelligence algorithm falls under the category of meta-
heuristic framework, which are well-established optimization methods
known for their robust theoretical framework and impressive optimiza-
tion capabilities. Like its counterparts in the swarm intelligence family,
the black widow optimization approach (BWOA), as presented by Hayy-
olalam and Kazem ( 2020), pursues optimal solutions by emulating
the reproductive behaviour of black widow spiders. This behaviour
includes actions such as crossover, cannibalism, and mutation. The
BWOA is a nature-inspired optimization algorithm that emulates the
hunting habits of black widow spiders in order to tackle intricate
optimization tasks such as HTSWP. During the web building stage,
prospective solutions, symbolized as spiders, form webs within the
search region. These webs encompass various areas of the solution
area, resulting in a varied population of potential options. The hunt-
ing cycle emulates the predatory conduct of spiders as they navigate
and seek out potential prey. Within the method’s framework, this
stage entails the solutions systematically exploring the solution area,
in search of the best possible outcomes or enhancements to the ex-
isting population. The technique employs a system that updates the
solutions by evaluating their fitness using an objective function. Algo-
rithmic processes undergo adjustments or updates in reaction to their
effectiveness, hence providing an evolutionary element. Furthermore,
the connection between structures and prey is of utmost importance,
as it represents the exchange of information and cooperation across
different solutions. This communication may involve the exchange of
knowledge or the synchronization of motions in order to collectively
enhance the total effectiveness of searches. The settings for parameters
in BWOA consist of the group size (𝑁), which determines the amount of
spiders during every iteration, as well as the highest possible number of
iterations (𝑀𝑎𝑥𝐼𝑡𝑒𝑟 ), which specifies the whole execution time of the
method. Web building characteristics dictate the formation of spider
webs, impacting the variety and extent of the possible configurations.
The hunting parameters regulate the process of exploration as well
as exploitation in spiders, determining their movement and search
strategies for finding the best solutions. The fitness value is a crucial
parameter that determines the goal that the strategy aims to optimize.
Like other optimizations techniques, it is crucial to carefully adjust
these variables, as their ideal values can differ based on the particular
optimizations problem being addressed. The BWOA is characterized by
its swift convergence rate and high level of optimization accuracy.
The operational steps of the BWOA can be outlined as follows:
• Step 1. The BWOA commences by creating a population of ran-
dom spiders. The step represents each spider entity through a
possible solution vector.
• Step 2. The fitness function of the problem is specifically designed
to assess the effectiveness of the solution. When robust offspring
